# Activation Clause

Maintains a document’s party roster, acceptance boundary and access guard. Business processing depends on participant access and acceptance of current terms. Hosted bootstrap resolves account locators into authenticated transports before initialization. As a root-local `Clause`, executable hooks come from its admitted exact type; paths below belong to the document where it executes.

## Configuration

Configuration is supplied through `parameters`; runtime operations read `/clauses/activation/parameters`.

- `parties` must be a nonempty object keyed by party name. Each party needs `lead/channel`. Party names and optional `representatives` keys are validated; their exact naming rules are inherited and not shown.
- `required` identifies parties whose acceptance is needed and defaults to all configured party keys. Negotiation requires a nonempty set.
- `accessPaths` defaults to `[]` and identifies embedded access documents to process and watch. `readers` defaults to `{}` and contributes to access checks. These defaults do not establish public access.
- `allowNewParties` defaults to `false` and controls additions through `updateParty_<role>`. `frozen` defaults to `false`; initial roster state is also frozen when `/partyRosterFrozen` is `true`.
- `revision` defaults to `1` and supplies the initial Activation revision.
- `preActivationOperations` and `preActivationChannels` default to `[]`. Party approval and update operations, plus generated negotiation operations, are automatically included among operations allowed before activation. These exceptions still require access and an open document.
- `negotiation/allowedPaths` defaults to `[]`; a nonempty list enables negotiation. Entries must be unique absolute paths with no empty segments or `~`. They cannot start under `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `type`, `name` or `description`, or equal or descend from an `accessPaths` entry. Each selected field must exist and be text, integer, double or boolean. The executing document must have `/type`, against which candidate terms are validated.
- `admission/approvers` must be nonempty for the approved-admission function to proceed. The supplied code does not establish the admission voting procedure.

Conflicting generated channel or contract names are rejected; an identical existing channel can be reused during planning. While configured negotiation has not reached first activation, changes to `/clauses` are rejected with `NEGOTIATION_POLICY_LOCKED`. Activation-clause changes through ordinary clause transitions are rejected with `USE_ACTIVATION_PARTY_OPERATIONS`.

## State and processing guard

`/activation` holds `parties`, `required`, per-party `approved` flags, revision counters, access information, terms and negotiation state. Initial `approved` and `accessRequests` are empty objects; `/partyAccess` starts as an empty collection for embedded access histories.

`accessReady` and `functional` record the same access-check result. That check includes parties in pending `accessRequests` whose `expectedRevision` matches the current revision, so preparing an admission can affect readiness before newcomers are admitted. `termsAccepted` requires acceptance from every `required` party and a successful current-terms check. Missing approval entries count as unaccepted during this computation. `active` additionally requires access readiness and that `closed` is not true. `everActivated` records whether activation has ever occurred and remains true afterward.

`status` distinguishes:

- `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`: access is unavailable before first activation.
- `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`: access is unavailable after activation has occurred.
- `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE`: access is ready, but acceptance or terms currency is incomplete.
- `ACTIVE`: access and acceptance conditions hold and the document is open.
- `CLOSED`: `closed` is true, taking precedence over the other statuses.

`reason` reports `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` or an empty string; an empty reason alone does not establish activation. Initialization defaults describe initialized state, not the meaning of missing observed values.

Refresh runs after `Clauses Initialized`, watched `Timeline Access Updated` events and party-addition request processing. Initial party transports remain pending until access is ready. State commits emit `Document Activated` on first activation, `Document Access Suspended` when an active document loses access, and `Document Access Restored` when it becomes active again after access was unavailable; these events carry `revision`.

The dispatch guard allows initialization and recognized embedded access-control deliveries to proceed even when ordinary processing is blocked. Other deliveries require initialized `/activation`, `accessReady` equal to true, a fresh access check and an open document. Configured pre-activation exceptions then pass this guard; remaining deliveries require `businessReady`, otherwise reporting `DOCUMENT_NOT_ACTIVE`. The detailed `accessValid`, `termsCurrent` and `businessReady` predicates are inherited and not supplied here.

A denied delivery runs no handlers. Denied external inputs are still consumed and checkpointed, and are not replayed when conditions change. Other installed dispatch policies can also deny delivery.

## Party acceptance and updates

`approve_<role>` accepts terms for the invoking party lead. It requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be true, a party channel, the current `/activation/revision` in `revision`, and valid participant access. With negotiation enabled, `termsRef` must identify `/activation/terms/ref`; any supplied reference is checked even without negotiation. Stale revisions or changed terms are rejected.

A new approval sets that party’s `approved` flag, commits state and emits `Terms Accepted` with `party` and `revision`. Repeating an existing approval is a no-op after validation. A successful approval does not by itself establish that the document is active. If this approval produces activation, a pending proposal is closed as `SUPERSEDED` and `negotiation/editable` becomes false.

`updateParty_<role>` takes `replacement`, including `lead/channel`, and optional `party`. Omitting `party` targets the invoking party. It requires exact-document review but no request `revision`. An existing party lead may update its own party, or add a new explicitly named party when `allowNewParties` permits it; it cannot replace another existing party. Frozen rosters, invalid names, missing lead channels, insufficient access for the resulting roster and contract-name conflicts are rejected.

A successful update installs the resulting roster contracts, clears all approvals, increments `revision` and emits `Party Changed`. A newly added party is appended to `required`. When an existing terms identity is affected by changed `parties` or `required`, the commit renews that identity, increments `termsRevision` and closes any pending proposal as `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`.

## Terms and negotiation

`/activation/terms/fields` stores negotiable values keyed by their document paths. `terms/definition` identifies the initial document after excluding negotiable values, configured access-document contents, Activation `accessPaths` and `readers`, and configured party `readerKeys`. `terms/ref` identifies the combination of that definition and those field values. `termsRevision` starts at `1`; negotiation starts with `revision: 1`, `editable: true`, and empty `proposal`, `history` and `outcomes` objects.

The following operations are generated with `_<role>` suffixes for configured required approvers. Every negotiation operation requires exact-document review and an invoking channel present in the current `/activation/required`.

- `proposeChanges_<role>` takes a unique `proposalId`, current `baseTermsRef`, and a nonempty `changes` list. Each change requires `path` and `replacement`. Paths must be allowed and nonduplicated, replacements must retain the current value’s kind, and the resulting document must match its declared type. Unchanged terms and reused closed proposal identifiers are rejected. Replacing a different pending proposal requires `supersedes` to identify it; the old proposal becomes `SUPERSEDED`.
- `proposeAndActivate_<role>` records the proposal and also invokes the caller’s acceptance of its proposed terms. Its name does not guarantee immediate activation.
- `activate_<role>` selects terms through `termsRef`. Current terms require omission of `proposalId` and route through ordinary approval using the current revision. Proposed terms require the matching proposal identifier and reference. The stored offer is revalidated against its base terms, allowed fields, document type and terms identity before proposal approval proceeds.
- `withdrawAcceptance_<role>` uses the same current-versus-proposed terms selection. It clears only the caller’s acceptance in `approved` or the proposal’s `approvals`.
- `withdrawProposal_<role>` and `rejectProposal_<role>` require the current `proposalId`, record `WITHDRAWN` or `REJECTED`, and clear the pending proposal. Withdrawal additionally requires the caller to be its `proposer`.

Proposal recording and approval completion delegate to inherited amendment functions whose detailed rules are not supplied. When that process reports completion, proposed values are applied to their document paths, `terms/ref` is replaced, both `termsRevision` and Activation `revision` increase, proposal approvals become Activation approvals, `editable` becomes false, and the outcome is `APPLIED`. State is then committed under the activation conditions above. A successful call or an individual proposal approval is not sufficient evidence of application.

`history` marks closed proposal identifiers; `outcomes` distinguishes application from withdrawal, rejection, supersession or authority change. New proposals, proposal closure and acceptance withdrawal are rejected after `everActivated` becomes true. Current-term `activate` still routes through ordinary approval.

## Admission and access requests

`Party Addition Requested` carries an approved admission’s roster and native Timeline Access documents in `accessDocuments`, keyed by party or `party__representative` transport name. Processing ignores stale `expectedRevision` values and already-recorded `admissionRef` values, checks the supplied access documents and installs their public histories under `/partyAccess`.

For existing parties whose access check fails against the expanded reader groups, it records requests under `/activation/accessRequests/<admissionRef>/requests` and emits `Party Access Update Requested`. Each request identifies the party, channel, access-document path, expected revision and access-entry identity, required `readerGroups`, and a `ready` flag subsequently refreshed from access checks. These requests neither grant private timeline access nor provide owner authority or participant consent. `Timeline Access Updated` confirms completion of an access update operation; current permissions come from the completed access document.

The separate `admitApprovedParties` function rejects frozen rosters, stale revisions, missing admission policy, invalid names, unavailable participant access and contract conflicts. It also invokes inherited main-party comparison checks whose criteria are not supplied. An unchanged resulting roster returns `duplicate`; a changed roster installs contracts, increments `revision`, commits state and emits `Party Changed` with `kind: Participants admitted` and `admissionRef`.

This admission route preserves `required` and does not unconditionally clear approvals. A roster authority change does clear approvals when negotiation is enabled and renews the terms identity as described above. An addition request therefore remains distinct from completed admission.
